pages.title: Cellular aging mechanisms

concepts.label: Cellular aging mechanisms
concepts.detail:
Cellular aging: Mechanisms


INTRINSIC                EXTRINSIC
Visual transcription: Intrinsic genetic factors: DNA repair defects -> accumulated mutations; genetic abnormalities (e.g. IGF-1 pathway) -> abnormal cellular signaling. Extrinsic environmental insults -> free radical-mediated damage, and reduced proteasomal activity -> damaged cellular proteins/organelles accumulate. Replicative senescence -> reduced new-cell production. These routes converge on cellular aging.
concepts.rationale: Explicit source definition, mechanism, comparison, condition or labelled example.

pages.title: Cell injury morphology diagram

concepts.label: Cell injury morphology diagram
concepts.detail: Visual transcription: Healthy cell Na/K ATPase exchanges 3 Na outward and 2 K inward. Hypoxia and ATP reduction accompany reversible cell/organelle swelling, detached ribosomes, chromatin clumping, blebbing, myelin figures; intracellular Na/osmotic pressure and Ca rise, K decreases. Irreversible injury: membrane rupture, nuclear pyknosis/karyorrhexis/karyolysis, vacuolization, amorphous mitochondrial densities, lysosomal rupture -> cell lysis.

pages.title: Calcium homeostasis

concepts.label: Calcium homeostasis
concepts.detail:
Loss of calcium homeostasis
•   Cytosolic        is normally Ca2+
    maintained by ATP-
    dependent       transportersCa2+
•   Injury allows a net influx of
    extracellular       across the Ca2+
    plasma membrane,
    followed by the release of
Ca2+from the intracellular
    stores.
•   Cell injury results in
    increased intracellular
    cytosolic     Ca2+
Visual transcription: Ca influx from extracellular space and release from mitochondria/smooth ER increases cytosolic Ca. Phospholipase -> decreased phospholipids; protease -> disrupted membrane/cytoskeleton proteins; these cause membrane damage. Endonuclease -> nuclear damage. ATPase -> decreased ATP. Ca also increases mitochondrial permeability transition -> decreased ATP.
